note: Wind was being counted as descent. The landing rate was the speed over the ground, which under a parachute includes the whole of the horizontal wind drift - so the app added the wind to your descent and judged the total against a 20 ft/s limit that means descent. With a 5 m/s wind that check could only be passed by a rocket descending under 11.4 ft/s, so every correctly sized main failed it on a windy day, and worst on the slowest and safest canopies. IF YOU HAVE EVER BEEN TOLD A ROCKET LANDS TOO FAST IN WIND, RE-FLY IT. Measured on a real 4 inch dual-deploy design, same rocket and canopy with only the wind changed: 3.39 m/s at no wind, 4.52 at 3 m/s, 6.04 at 5 m/s - exactly the square root of descent squared plus wind squared. That rocket descends at 13.3 ft/s and was reported at 20.9. The recovery table now shows the vertical descent rate and a separate 'Over ground' column, and the drogue band is judged on descent too.
